title: Customer escalation: action_output byte-shift after multibyte chunk split in reverse-proxy retry
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Production customer reported repeated occurrences where structured tool responses (field name: action_output) arrive with shifted bytes resulting in invalid JSON keys and truncated string values. Issue occurs when requests are proxied from Hosted frontends to Dedicated backends through the regional gateway; failures correlate with gateway retry events and with responses containing multi-byte UTF-8 characters (e.g., emoji, CJK).

Observed behavior: In affected traces the JSON stream shows a single byte offset starting at an early chunk boundary, e.g. '"actiȯn_output"' or '"action_output\uFFFD...' and subsequent parser failure. Downstream consumers (Console, callbacks) see parse errors and sometimes receive partial data. Customer impact: production feature regression for two enterprise customers driving escalations — chat features occasionally drop tool output or mis-map fields causing incorrect actions and loss of critical metadata.

Repro steps (internal):
1) Use hosted gateway to send long assistant response with tool call including multibyte content in one of the tool fields.
2) Enable gateway retry simulation with small MTU/chunk size configuration to force chunk-splitting on multibyte code points.
3) Observe structured JSON stream reassembled at the Dedicated backend and note byte offset introduced at chunk boundary when retry occurs.

Hypothesis / root cause: The regional gateway's streaming retry logic replays partial chunks but does not align split boundaries to UTF-8 code point boundaries. When a retry inserts or splices a segment that begins or ends inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character, the reassembly logic in the reverse proxy uses naive byte concatenation and a downstream chunk-merging heuristic then hands the stream to the parser which treats the broken sequence as valid bytes. Our parser's lenient chunk-concat path attempts in-place repair (replacement character) in some paths and in others shifts subsequent bytes when trimming invalid leading bytes, causing a field-name shift rather than a simple replacement. Edge case surfaces only when: (a) gateway retry occurs, (b) payload contains multi-byte characters crossing the injected boundary, (c) reassembly goes through the legacy fast-path that bypasses full utf8 sanitation for performance.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Rolled out a gateway config toggle to disable aggressive retry-on-stream-chunk for affected customers (hosted region-us-west-2) — mitigates new occurrences but not yet applied globally.
- Temporary server-side parser guard added to detect invalid UTF-8 sequences at chunk boundaries and fail-safe to request re-transmit rather than silently reassemble. This guard was shipped behind a flag (parser.strict_boundary_check=true) and enabled for the two impacted tenants.

Planned fix:
1) Patch proxy replay logic to ensure replayed segments align to UTF-8 code point boundaries: when splitting chunks, the proxy must find code point boundaries and, if needed, extend the chunk window to include full code points before replaying.
2) Replace legacy fast-path reassembly with a corrected streaming reassembler that enforces code point alignment and uses a small buffer to hold incomplete characters until the next chunk arrives.
3) Add end-to-end unit + fuzz tests that create random multi-byte splits and simulate retries so regressions are caught in CI.
4) Backfill parser tests and add an integration test that runs against a staging gateway configured to simulate retries.

Rollout plan: Patch will be in runtime-1.22. Patch candidate will be staged to a canary fleet in us-west-2 for 48 hours with telemetry checks. If stable, promote to regional gateways across Hosted and Dedicated proxies. For Private deployments, publish advisory and patch release with applied zero-downtime instructions for operators.

Monitoring and metrics: Added a dashboard tile showing 'stream-retry-utf8-errors' and a trace tag 'replay_boundary_detected' to correlate traces. Pager alert created for >0.05% of requests with parser.strict_failure in a 5m window.

Why this is unique: Unlike earlier issues that were due to delimiter loss or JSON token reordering, this bug is caused by low-level byte alignment problems across multibyte encodings during proxy replay and interacts with a legacy fast-path that attempted to optimize reassembly. Fix requires changes in proxy replay and in the reassembly safety net in the runtime.
comments: 2026-03-05 Aisha: Initial report from X-enterprise support — customer provides raw capture and points to field name corruption. Marked P0 and assigned to Liam.
2026-03-06 Liam: Reproduced locally with gateway simulation. Confirmed byte offset at chunk boundary when multibyte char spans split. Started prototype patch for proxy boundary alignment.
2026-03-07 Eng-Infra: Reviewed patch; asked to ensure compatibility with existing HTTP/2 frame handling; noted potential perf impact of checking code points on hot path.
2026-03-09 Design Review: Decided to implement a small lookahead buffer to avoid per-byte decoding on the hot path. Trade-off: modest memory per-stream vs throughput impact; engineering accepts.
2026-03-11 Ops: Enabled parser.strict_boundary_check=true for two affected tenants in us-west-2. Customer reports immediate decrease in incidents.
2026-03-12 QA: Integration tests added to CI; fuzz harness producing repeatable failure cases. No regression detected in latency within 1% for typical payloads after lookahead buffer implementation.
2026-03-13 Liam: Preparing PR and release notes. Requesting 2 approvers from Infra and Runtime teams before canary deploy.
2026-03-13 PM note: Coordinate customer comms — provide timeline for fix and mitigation steps for Private customers.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for codepoint-aligned splitting; 2) Fuzz harness integrating gateway retry simulator for 1000 randomized runs; 3) Integration test against staging gateway with strict_boundary_check toggled; 4) Load test to verify <2% p50 latency regression on streaming hot path.
postmortem_actions: 1) Add a pre-deploy checklist item for streaming replay changes that enumerates encoding boundary guarantees. 2) Ship advisory for Private customers and include patch notes. 3) Run a one-week retrospective with Infra and Runtime to identify other fast-paths that bypass encoding validation. 4) Expand observability for 'replay_boundary_detected' in support runbooks.
release_notes_blurb: Fix: prevent occasional structured output corruption when gateway retries split multi-byte characters across stream chunks. This resolves customer-reported JSON parse failures and action mapping errors in Hosted and Dedicated deployments.
